- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) are common; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 7 days’ sentiment-weighted price to adjust forecast baseline.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment turn.
